newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia's leader worried about Mideast peace.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia's leader worried about Mideast peace.

text.p: Tunisia's President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali on Friday urged the world community "to work actively and firmly" to save peace and thwart the dangers facing the Middle East.
The official TAP news agency quoted Ben Ali, who was addressing diplomats accredited to Tunis, as saying that he was deeply concerned by Israel's anti-peace policies.

"We are deeply concerned by the obstruction of the Middle East peace process, the freezing of the agreements on which it is based and the dangerous deadlock because of Israel's persistence in its policy of settlement in Al-Quds (Jerusalem) and elsewhere".
Ben Ali urged the international community to "work actively and firmly to save peace and thwart the dangers" that weigh on the region in order to regain the legitimate rights of Palestinians.
Ben Ali did not refer to two Arab suicide attacks in Jerusalem's main Jewish market on Wednesday in which 13 people were killed.
He also called for the setting up of "an independent Palestinian state with Arab East Jerusalem as its capital, and for Syria and Lebanon to recover their occupied land from Israel.
